shared.name: anonymous function expressions end a value
async and generator expressions end values
shared.code: const a = async function () {} / 2; const b = function* () {} / 3;

shared.name: async and generator declarations permit regex statements
class declarations permit regex statements
anonymous and named class expressions end values

shared.name: class heritage expressions retain their nested bodies
nested object methods preserve their enclosing expression

shared.name: declarations inside blocks retain statement position
export default function and class declarations permit regex statements
labels and control statements permit regex statements
for await body starts a statement
shared.code: async function read() { for await (const item of items) /value/.test(item); }

shared.name: parenthesized arrows and object values still use division
function expressions cannot consume a host closing brace as regex text
escaped function names retain their complete spelling
escaped members and Unicode code points do not split tokens
escaped and non-ASCII class names retain complete spans
incomplete function expression inside template preserves its boundary
a line break after return begins a new declaration
line breaks separate declarations from previous values
computed class members and static blocks preserve the enclosing body
shared.code: class Example { [name]() { return /inside/; } static { const value = class {} / 2; } } /after/.test(value);
